title: Taking away
examples: Teacher, if I have five apples and I eat two, how many are left?
What do I do when I take some things away from a group?
Can you show me taking away with my fingers?

explain.say: Look at the picture. You can see five red balloons.
Two balloons float away. Three balloons are left.
You started with five. You took away two. Three are left.
You have seven stickers. You give three to a friend. Count back: six, five, four.
Taking away means finding how many are left.

items: Start with a group of things

explain.say: You have ten crayons. You give four to Mei. Six crayons are left.

faq.a: Taking away means subtraction. It tells us how many are left when some are removed from a group.
asks: How do I find how many are left?

faq.q: Is taking away always the same as counting backwards?
faq.a: Yes, for small numbers, counting backwards is a great way to help you take away. You just count down from the starting number.
asks: Can I count backwards to take away?

faq.q: Do I need to know my number facts to take away?
faq.a: Number facts help. You can also use your fingers or draw pictures.
asks: What if I forget my number facts?
Can I use my fingers for subtraction?

faq.q: Does the order matter when I take away?
faq.a: Yes, the order matters a lot. Taking away two from five is not the same as taking away five from two.
asks: Is 5 minus 2 the same as 2 minus 5?
Does the big number always go first?

faq.q: What if I take away more than I have?
faq.a: With real things, you can only take away what you have. If you take them all away, zero are left.
asks: Can I take away ten from three?
What is the answer if I take away too much?

facts: Subtraction is the process of taking one number away from another.
The symbol for taking away is the minus sign.
If you start with a group and take some away, you find how many are left.

quiz.say: Look at the stars. Take away three. How many stars are left?
quiz.why: Count back three from eight: seven, six, five.

wrong.0: Six is one too many, so count back three steps from eight.
wrong.2: Eleven is eight add three, but here you take away.

quiz.say: Hold up ten fingers. Hide four fingers. How many fingers can you see?
quiz.why: Ten take away four leaves six fingers.

wrong.1: Seven is one too many, so count the fingers you can see again.
wrong.2: Fourteen is ten add four, but here you take away.

quiz.say: Read the sum. Take away zero. How many are left?
quiz.why: Taking away zero takes nothing. All four are still there.

wrong.0: Three would be four take away one, but you take away zero.
wrong.1: Zero is the number you take away, so the four are all still there.
